# slack-waterline

> A Claude Code skill that reads every message in a Slack workspace and proves
> nothing was missed, then writes the daily or weekly digest and, when asked,
> the reply. Zero dependencies, many workspaces from one install.

The core idea: a read position may only move for content that was actually
delivered to a reader. Fetching is not reading. Three positions are tracked per
conversation — what was READ, what the triage SCORED, and what SLACK is holding
— each with exactly one writer.

The problem it solves: a Slack reply never moves its parent message, so a
conversation happening inside an older thread reports zero unread from the top
level. Most catch-up tooling also marks messages read when it fetches them,
which turns any interruption into a permanent silent loss.

## Docs

- [SKILL.md](skills/slack-waterline/SKILL.md): the operating instructions an agent follows
- [setup.md](skills/slack-waterline/references/setup.md): getting a token from zero — manifest, browser-driven, or by hand
- [read-state.md](skills/slack-waterline/references/read-state.md): the three read positions and the misses that motivated each
- [tokens-and-scopes.md](skills/slack-waterline/references/tokens-and-scopes.md): user vs bot tokens, scope list, rate limits, the HTTP 200 trap
- [workspace-config.md](skills/slack-waterline/references/workspace-config.md): per-workspace config, signal patterns, running many workspaces
- [reports.md](skills/slack-waterline/references/reports.md): digest format, delivery to your own DM, scheduling
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): invariants for anyone modifying the skill
- [README.md](README.md): install and usage
